statement: Fix a locally $\mathfrak U$-small category $\mathcal M$ with $\mathfrak U$-small filtered colimits and a $\mathfrak U$-small set $I=C_0$ of arrows. The desired factorization is $f=pi$ with $p\in I^\perp$ and $i\in{}^\perp(I^\perp)$.
notes: Program of (1.1)--(1.2); proved in the corrected form of Theorem 1 below.

statement: A functorial factorization is a section $\Phi_\alpha:\mathcal M^{[1]}\to\mathcal M^{[2]}$ of composition, with middle-object functor $X_\alpha$ and natural maps $i_\alpha,p_\alpha$ satisfying $p_\alpha i_\alpha=f$.
notes: (1.3)--(1.9); the source uses Nerf_1,Nerf_2 for arrow and composable-pair categories.

statement: For a square $(u_X,u_Y):f\to f^{\prime}$, functoriality means $X_\alpha(u)i_\alpha(f)=i_\alpha(f^{\prime})u_X$ and $p_\alpha(f^{\prime})X_\alpha(u)=u_Yp_\alpha(f)$.
notes: (1.10)--(1.11); equivalent componentwise description of naturality.

statement: The initial stage is $X_0(f)=X$, $i_0(f)=1_X$, $p_0(f)=f$.
notes: Recursion clause 1.

statement: The successor stage is $X_{\alpha+1}(f)=X_1(p_\alpha(f))$, $i_{\alpha+1}=i_1(p_\alpha)i_\alpha$, and $p_{\alpha+1}=p_1(p_\alpha)$. Its immediate transition is $i_1(p_\alpha(f))$.
notes: Recursion clause 2 and (1.12).

statement: At a nonzero limit ordinal $\lambda$, $X_\lambda=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}X_\beta$, with $i_\lambda$ and $p_\lambda$ induced by the compatible maps from $X$ and to $Y$.
notes: Recursion clause 3. The phrase limite projective des p_beta can be understood through Hom(colim X_beta,Y)=lim Hom(X_beta,Y); it is not a different limit construction.

statement: A pointed endofunctor $(P,\eta)$ of $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ over codomain determines the continuous transfinite system of factorizations, using filtered colimits in each slice $\mathcal M/Y$.
gap_or_error: The naturality and coherence of the transfinite construction are not expanded.
repair: The commentary gives induction on successors and the universal property at limits; no monad structure is required.
notes: (1.13)--(1.14). Chosen colimit cocones give actual functors, unique up to canonical natural isomorphism.

statement: Fact$(I)$ says that each square $D:j\to f$ with $j\in I$ gives a factorization $X\to X\amalg_A B\to Y$ admitting a map to $X\to X_1(f)\to Y$ under $X$ and over $Y$.
notes: (1.15); formulated when the indicated pushouts exist.

statement: An arrow $j:A\to B$ is pushoutable (coquarrable) if $X\amalg_A B$ exists for every map $A\to X$. The construction assumes every member of $I$ is pushoutable.
notes: (1.16); the word also defines coquarrable.

statement: When the required pushouts exist, Fact$(I)$ is equivalent to: every square $(a,b):j\to f$ admits $h:B\to X_1(f)$ with $hj=i_1(f)a$ and $p_1(f)h=b$. The latter property is meaningful without pushouts.
notes: (1.17); equivalence by the pushout universal property.

statement: For every $j\in I$ and square against $p_\alpha(f)$, the lifting problem becomes solvable after the transition $X_\alpha(f)\to X_{\alpha+1}(f)$.
notes: Corollary 1 of (1.17). The requirement j in I is inherited from (1.17), though not repeated in its displayed statement.

references: SGA4I1972, I Definition 9.1; Riehl2014, Theorem 12.2.2; commentary block Why the cofinality bound solves every problem
notes: Counterexample: in Set, I={empty->1,fold:2->1}, f=id_1; X_1=2 and p_1:2->1 is not I-injective, while I_1={0} is grand devant every pi.

statement: A Quillen precouple is a pair $(\Phi,\Psi)$ of classes of maps with $\Phi\subset{}^{\square}\Psi$ and every map $f$ admitting $f=pi$, $i\in\Phi$, $p\in\Psi$.

statement: A precouple is closed when both classes are fixed by their respective lifting closure operators; a closed precouple is called a Quillen couple.
notes: Definition4.1 and sentence at ms29.

statement: For a precouple, closedness is equivalent to $\Phi={}^{\square}\Psi$ and $\Psi=\Phi^{\square}$.

statement: For a Quillen precouple and a map $j$, the following are equivalent: $j\in\widetilde\Phi$; $j\in{}^{\square}\Psi$; $j$ is a retract of a map of $\Phi$; such a retract can be taken with the same source; every factorization $j=pi$ with $p\in\Psi$ admits $q$ with $pq=1$ and $qj=i$.

statement: A precouple is closed if and only if both classes are closed under retracts in the arrow category.
notes: Proposition4.2 Corollary2. Closing both classes under retracts always gives a weak factorization system.

statement: Lemma 5.3: In a category with equalizers, $f:Z\to Y$ is epic iff it does not factor through a noninvertible strict monomorphism into $Y$.
gap_or_error: The printed arrow is named f and then twice called g; strict must retain the categorical sense of SGA 4, not mean an arbitrary proper subobject.
repair: A strict monomorphism which is epic is invertible; if f is not epic, an equalizer of distinct arrows equal after f is a proper strict subobject through which f factors.

statement: $(d_0)$: Each $\mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}$ is closed under colimits indexed by a category with at most $\pi$ arrows.

repair: If the target is bounded use subobject closure; if the source is bounded use the quotient onto its image. Conversely, the image of a monomorphism is its domain and the image-full quotient clause is precisely the remaining case.

statement: The hypothesis of Corollary 5.4 holds when $\pi\ge\pi_1$ and $\pi^{\pi_0}=\pi$, in particular for suitable $\pi=2^c$.
notes: Uses the uniform object accessibility estimate, not the incorrect Hom-count bounds later in Section 3.

statement: Scholie 5.5: Under either reconstruction hypothesis the subobject diagram gives a canonical $\pi^+$-directed presentation of $X$; under $(e)$ it is perfectly $\pi$-adapted.
repair: A pi-small directed colimit of bounded subobjects is bounded by (d_0) and remains monic by (e), so it is their supremum.

statement: For an isomorphism-invariant class $M$, put $M^\pi=M\cap\mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}$.
If $M$ satisfies $b_\pi$ of Chapter XIII, then $X\in M$ iff its $M^\pi$-subobjects are cofinal in $\operatorname{Sub}_{\pi}(X)$, whenever the canonical subobject presentation is perfectly adapted.
notes: This is (5.1); the surrounding argument uses (e) for perfect adaptation.

statement: For any isomorphism-invariant $S\subset\mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}$, the class defined by cofinality of its S-subobjects restricts to S on $\mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}$.
repair: A bounded X is the largest member of its bounded-subobject poset, so cofinality forces the largest member to be good.
notes: This is (5.2).

statement: The criterion (5.1) alone need not imply $\pi$-accessibility.
repair: The stronger criterion (5.3) already fails to imply accessibility by the explicit two-point-poset example in our p55 block; that example therefore also proves this assertion.

statement: A $\pi$-accessible class must contain the retracts of its bounded members.
repair: Realize the retract as a highly directed colimit of the idempotent; equivalently use the perfectly adapted presentation with original object at successor stages and its retract at limit stages. Cofinal original stages force the retract into M by b_pi.

statement: Criterion (5.3): for every closed cofinal $J\subset\operatorname{Sub}_{\pi}(X)$, $X\in M$ iff the M-members of J are cofinal in J; closed means closed under directed suprema of subsets of cardinal at most $\pi$.
Footnote 20: Replacing cofinality of J by the condition that its subobject diagram has colimit X strengthens (5.3), and gives an equivalent condition when the bounded objects are $\pi$-accessible.
repair: Under the retained closure condition J is pi-adapted and hence pi^+-directed; Corollary 5.4 then supplies cofinality. The converse is the ordinary finality property of colimits.

statement: Proposition 5.6 as first stated: at a rank where bounded objects are $\pi$-accessible, condition (5.3) alone is equivalent to $b_\pi$.
gap_or_error: Subobject presentations cannot detect nontrivial retracts of a fixed object when the candidate class is not retract-closed.
repair: Grothendieck retracts the assertion in footnote 21 and on ms pp.54–55, adding closure of M^pi under pi-small filtered colimits. Our p55 development realizes the proposed counterexample in Pos.
notes: Source-recognized failure; do not report as a later discovery.

statement: Lemma 5.7: In a perfectly $\pi$-adapted presentation of X, at a rank where bounded objects are $\pi$-accessible and under $(e)$, the stages mapping monomorphically into X are cofinal.
gap_or_error: Factoring the image U_i→X through a stage does not yet make the composite X_i→U_i→X_j equal the transition.
repair: Use accessibility of X_i to pass to a later stage where this equality holds; iterate and take the countable supremum. Full proof in our p57 block.

statement: The monomorphic stage indices of Lemma 5.7 are closed under directed suprema of subsets of cardinal at most $\pi$.
repair: Use perfect adaptation and closure of monomorphisms under filtered colimits (e).

statement: The proof applies (5.3) directly to the image J of the monomorphic stage indices in $\operatorname{Sub}_{\pi}(X)$.
gap_or_error: The hypotheses ensure cofinality of J, but its closure under pi-small directed suprema does not follow. Images of continuous monotone maps can fail this closure.
repair: Under the corrected small-colimit closure of M^pi, alternate monomorphic stages with good small subobjects and take a countable supremum. This proves cofinality of good stages without assuming J is closed. Our p57 block also gives an explicit perfectly adapted Set diagram whose image is not closed.
notes: The false item is this inference, not the corrected Proposition 5.6.

statement: If a bounded object $X_0$ has no monic endomorphism other than the identity, the class of objects isomorphic to $X_0$ satisfies (5.3).
repair: For X≅X_0 any cofinal J contains X. Conversely, a cofinal system of X_0-subobjects has only isomorphisms as transitions, and therefore has colimit X_0.

statement: Such an $X_0$ may have a nontrivial idempotent with image not isomorphic to $X_0$, so its isomorphism class need not be $\pi$-accessible.
repair: Take the two-element chain in Pos and the constant endomorphism at its least element; full verification including an adapted diagram in our p55 block.

statement: With closure of $M^\pi$ under filtered colimits of cardinal at most $\pi$, condition (5.3) is equivalent to $b_\pi$ under the hypotheses of corrected Proposition 5.6.
repair: Good indices of an adapted diagram are closed under small directed suprema. Use the repaired Lemma 5.7 and the alternating comparison given in our p57 block. This also repairs the raw-image step on p53.

statement: Proposition 5.7: Under $(a)$–$(e)$ and $\pi$-accessibility of all bounded objects, the following are equivalent: (a) $b_\pi$ plus all filtered-colimit closure; (b) $b_\pi$ plus pi-small filtered-colimit closure of the bounded part; (c) recognition by cofinally many subobjects in a pi-small-filtered-colimit-closed bounded class.
gap_or_error: Condition (c) uses an undefined J, intended to be Ss_pi(X). The proof of arbitrary filtered-colimit closure is only sketched in Proposition 5.9.
repair: Set J=Ss_pi(X). The p57 and p60 blocks prove the corrected recognition equivalence; the p65 block completes the needed good-rank case of Proposition 5.9.

statement: In condition (c) of Proposition 5.7, the chosen bounded class is exactly $M\cap\mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}$.
repair: Test the criterion on bounded objects, where the subobject poset has its largest element.

statement: Printed condition (cprime): M is the smallest class closed under filtered colimits, with no stated requirement to contain M_0.
gap_or_error: The words contenant M_0 are omitted, so the literal smallest class is empty regardless of M_0.
repair: Read M as the smallest isomorphism-invariant class containing M_0 and closed under small filtered colimits. This intended fourth condition is proved with the other three at the good rank; source words retained.

statement: With the missing containment restored, condition (cprime) is equivalent to (a),(b),(c) at the rank specified in Proposition 5.7, and M_0 may be chosen small.
repair: Close M_0 under pi-small filtered colimits inside Filt^pi, apply the recognition theorem, and use its minimality. Take representatives in the essentially small bounded level. Full argument in our p60 block.

statement: Corollary 5.8: $M\mapsto M\cap\mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}$ and the cofinal-small-subobject construction are inverse bijections between the classes in Proposition 5.7 and the bounded classes closed under pi-small filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: The parenthetical description of the least closed class again omits containing the bounded class.
repair: Restore the containment in the interpretation; proof follows from reconstruction and the largest-subobject test.

statement: Footnote 22 asks whether (cprime) implies (c) without the special object-accessibility assumption on pi.
repair: The verified proof here establishes the implication at the good ranks used in Proposition 5.7. No fixed-rank general proof or counterexample is claimed.
notes: Open records the source question; this audit does not assert that it remains an open research problem today.

statement: A pi-adapted poset is a nonempty directed poset admitting suprema of its directed subsets of cardinal at most pi. A pi-cofinal subset is cofinal and closed under these suprema.
notes: For infinite pi such a poset is pi^+-directed: close a pi-small set under chosen finite upper bounds, then take its directed supremum.

statement: Lemma 5.8: the intersection of two pi-cofinal subsets of a pi-adapted poset is pi-cofinal.
repair: Alternate choices in the two sets above a prescribed element; the two countable subsequences have the same supremum. Closure of the intersection is immediate.

statement: Condition (c) of Proposition 5.7 implies (5.3).
repair: The good small subobjects are closed under pi-small directed suprema by (e) and bounded filtered-colimit closure. Their intersection with any closed cofinal J is cofinal iff they themselves are cofinal; apply Lemma 5.8.

statement: Proposition 5.9 is stated under $(a),(b),(c),(d_0)$, for any pi≥pi_0: a b_pi-class M is closed under all filtered colimits iff its bounded part is closed under filtered colimits of cardinal at most pi.
gap_or_error: The written proof calls upon a subobject-based Lemma 5.10 although (d_1),(d_2),(e) have been dropped, and claims not to need a good rank.
repair: Complete proof in our p65 block under the extra condition that Filt^pi-objects are pi-accessible; it uses slices and small filtered subcategories and no image hypotheses. This is sufficient for Proposition 5.7. The unrestricted fixed-rank assertion is not settled in this audit.
notes: A limitation of verification is not a claim of falsity or of present-day openness.

statement: The necessity direction of Proposition 5.9 follows under exactly its stated hypotheses.
repair: A pi-small filtered colimit of M^pi-objects belongs to M by closure and to Filt^pi by (d_0).

statement: For a diagram Y:I→M, the pullback of the codomain functor $M^\pi/M\to M$ is the category of triples $(i,A,A\to Y_i)$; it is opfibred over I, with fibre $M^\pi/Y_i$.
repair: Cocartesian transport is postcomposition with Y(u), leaving A unchanged.

statement: Lemma 5.10: for Y∈M, the category $M^\pi/Y$ is filtered.
gap_or_error: The displayed proof uses the earlier image hypotheses, which are absent from the formally weaker Proposition 5.9.
repair: Under the section image hypotheses use good small subobjects. At good pi use factorization and eventual equality in an M^pi-presentation instead, as proved in our p65 block.

statement: The printed lemma and display assert that the unrestricted $\operatorname{Sub}_{\pi}(Y)$ maps canonically and cofinally into $M^\pi/Y$.
gap_or_error: A bounded subobject of Y need not belong to M, so the alleged functor is not generally defined.
repair: Use $\operatorname{Sub}_{\pi}^{M}(Y)$, as already required by the proof and printed correctly in the later NB. Under the image hypotheses it is filtered and final in M^pi/Y.
notes: The omission is an edition slip retained in the source text.

statement: For the corrected subobject functor, the finality tests F1 and F2 hold: every bounded-domain map factors through a good bounded subobject, and maps into a fixed subobject over Y are unique.
repair: Use its bounded image and (5.1) for F1; monicity makes F2 immediate.

statement: Corollary 5.11: if I is filtered and all Y_i belong to M^pi, the total category of triples is filtered and its projection to I is final.
repair: Move two objects to a common base index and find a common successor in the fibre. For parallel maps, first equalize their base arrows, then their vertical parts. The same construction proves finality of the projection.

statement: The form of Corollary 5.11 required in Proposition 5.9 allows Y_i∈M, not merely Y_i∈M^pi.
gap_or_error: The corollary is printed with the stronger M^pi hypothesis although the setup on p62 uses M.
repair: The same proof applies once filteredness and density of the fibres M^pi/Y_i have been established for Y_i∈M.

statement: The projection in Corollary 5.11 is described parenthetically as fibrant.
gap_or_error: The constructed codomain projection is an opfibration; a fibration would require unassumed pullback closure.
repair: Interpret cofibrant/opfibred, consistently with the preceding paragraph and explicit transport by postcomposition.

statement: If I is a poset, restricting the total category to good subobjects in each fibre yields a poset final in the total category.
repair: Every object factors vertically into a good small subobject; any two choices have a common larger choice. Morphisms between subobject triples are unique when they exist. This restriction need not itself be an opfibration.

statement: If every fibre source diagram has colimit Y_i, then the colimit of the source diagram over the total category is $\varinjlim_iY_i$.
repair: A cocone on the total category is exactly a compatible family of cocones on fibres; use their universal properties. Full ordinary-colimit calculation in our p64 block.

statement: For a filtered poset I, its directed subsets J of cardinal at most pi form a pi^+-directed poset P, and directed families of at most pi such J have their union as supremum.
repair: Close the union of at most pi subsets under chosen finite upper bounds by countably many steps. Infinite pi keeps cardinality at most pi. Directed unions remain directed.

statement: If $X_J=\varinjlim_{i\in J}X_i$ for the preceding subsets, then $X=\varinjlim_{J\in P}X_J$, and the diagram on P is perfectly pi-adapted.
repair: Compatible cocones on the pieces are precisely cocones on their union; the pieces cover every object and arrow of the original diagram.

statement: If all X_i∈M^pi and M^pi is closed under pi-small filtered colimits, then all X_J∈M^pi, hence the perfectly adapted presentation forces X∈M by b_pi.
notes: This final step needs no image hypothesis or good-rank assumption once the initial flattening into M^pi has been justified.

statement: Definition 5.12(1): M is L-pi-accessible if it satisfies b_pi and is closed under all small filtered colimits; L-stable means this latter closure.
Proposition 5.9 identifies L-pi-accessibility with b_pi plus closure of the bounded part under pi-small filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: At unrestricted pi this inherits the verification limitation in Proposition 5.9.
repair: The equivalence is completely verified here at a rank where every Filt^pi-object is pi-accessible.

statement: At a good pi, M is L-pi-accessible iff it is the filtered-colimit closure of a class contained in Filt^pi; every L-pi-accessible M has such a generating bounded part regardless of this extra condition.
gap_or_error: Definition 5.12 restates (a),(b),(c),(d) but drops (e), used in the cited Proposition 5.7.
repair: Sufficiency is completely proved here at good pi under (e), by Proposition 5.7. For necessity, b_pi supplies a cofinal diagram of M^pi-objects in an adapted presentation, and L-stability gives the reverse inclusion.
notes: No proof of sufficiency after removing (e) is claimed.

statement: Definition 5.12(2): M is L-accessible iff it is L-pi-accessible for some pi; equivalently, it is accessible and L-stable.
notes: Here accessible for a class means b_pi for some filtration rank, not an unqualified modern category definition.

statement: L-accessibility is equivalent to being the isomorphism-invariant filtered-colimit closure of an essentially small family M_0; M_0 can be chosen as a set of representatives.
gap_or_error: The cited classification was proved under (e), which the printed definition omits.
repair: Necessity uses the essentially small bounded part. Under (e), sufficiency follows by choosing a sufficiently large good cardinal containing the given family and applying Proposition 5.7.
notes: The equivalence under the weaker printed ambient hypotheses has not been independently established in this audit.

statement: A family of objects is bounded in the filtration iff its full subcategory is essentially small, up to replacement by isomorphic representatives.
repair: A bounded level is essentially small. Conversely choose a small representative set and a cardinal bounding all its filtration indices; the filtration is exhaustive and increasing.

statement: The notion of L-accessibility is independent of the chosen cardinal filtration.
repair: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.7, use the equivalent description as filtered-colimit closure of an essentially small family, which does not mention the filtration.
notes: This assertion concerns existence of some rank, not equality of fixed-rank notions for arbitrary filtrations. Removing (e) inherits the preceding verification limitation.

statement: Footnote 17 suggests that the arguments will need only $(d_2)$ and not $(d_1)$.
repair: The bounded-image constructions in Proposition 5.3 and the subsequent comparison proof indeed use (d_2). This suggestion must be distinguished from the separately false assertion that (d_2) implies (d_1).
notes: The commentary does not infer logical dependence of the axioms merely from their appearance in the stated hypotheses.

statement: Given the sufficiency direction of (5.1), it suffices in (5.3) to verify that X in M implies cofinality of the good members of each closed cofinal J.
repair: Conversely, if the good members are cofinal in J and J is cofinal among all bounded subobjects, the good bounded subobjects are cofinal; apply the assumed sufficiency direction of (5.1).

statement: Definition 5.12 is introduced under (a),(b),(c),(d), without restating (e).
gap_or_error: Its later small-generation equivalences invoke the earlier subobject recognition theorem, whose proof used (e).
repair: Keep the definition as printed, but state the proven classification under (e) and the good-rank condition. Our p66 commentary records this scope distinction explicitly.
notes: This is a limitation of the proof supplied here, not a counterexample or assertion of present-day openness.
